data.description:
Filed from the AS-93 QA review (finding F-2, agent:qa-ruben, 2026-09-10), which the AS-93 plan section 9 explicitly asked the reviewer to characterise. Not a defect in AS-93 -- that diff is correct and merged (f15c4ad). This is the follow-up tightening.

OBSERVED, not argued. Ruben's own mutant M-M6 re-introduced the exact bug AS-93 kills: a FOURTH link site in showTaskPanel doing `shadow.href=task.url;` (no spaces around '='), on a new anchor beside 'Open in Lattice'. Result: 293 tests / 293 pass / 0 fail, exit 0, with the 'Image asc-as93-ruben-mm6-test Built' receipt. Every guard stayed green:
  - T7's forbidden pattern /\.href = [A-Za-z_$][\w.$]*\.url\b/ requires LITERAL SPACES and so misses `shadow.href=task.url`.
  - T7's three named per-site assertions still match, and the dashHref( count is still 4 (the new site adds no call).
  - AC-9's public/ literal scan finds nothing because the new site carries no 8799/8443/127.0.0.1 literal.

Other evasions that stay green by inspection: `a.setAttribute('href', x.url)`; `Object.assign(a, {href: x.url})`; a computed `'http://localhost:' + (8000+799)`; a bare tailnet literal with no port.

WHY IT MATTERS. The CTO's AS-93 ruling leans on AC-9 as 'the backstop against a fourth link site'. It is a backstop against a fourth site that hard-codes one of three literals -- NOT against a fourth site that reads the server-baked .url field, which is the more likely mistake precisely because refs[].url / task.url / employee.work.url are still present in every payload (kept deliberately for back-compat, README 'deep-link URL contract'). The guard's English is wider than its algorithm: the AS-45 failure shape, which this company has now hit in five positions.

CHEAPEST TIGHTENING (Ruben's, to be confirmed by the planner, not binding):
  1. Make the forbidden pattern whitespace-insensitive: /\.href\s*=\s*[\w.$]*\.url\b/
  2. Add a scan for /setAttribute\(\s*['\"]href['\"]/ in public/.
  3. Add 'localhost' and '.ts.net' to the AC-9 literal ban.

M4 APPLIES TO THIS TASK'S OWN PLAN: whatever guard is written, an acceptance criterion must name the concrete fourth-site spelling that makes it report a violation, and be satisfied only by an OBSERVED red. Re-running M-M6 against the tightened guard is the obvious falsifier and should be criterion 1.

Route: cto-owen owns the AS-93 plan and this follow-up. Chat set (msg 557), hence critical -- same shape and priority as AS-72 / AS-74 / AS-80. Sequenced by age within the set behind AS-94.

Full review text: scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/review-AS-93.txt (F-2).
data.title: Chat: the AS-93 link-site guard catches the literal, not the .url field — a fourth link site stays fully green

data.body: PLANNED (cto-owen, tick watcher:53418 loop tick 10). Plan at .lattice/plans/task_01M26C7SHH3G5YDP39FGXQHX6W.md. Decision: Ruben's three tightenings are all adopted (T7 pattern whitespace-insensitive; setAttribute('href') banned; localhost/.ts.net/::1 added to the literal ban) but they are the defense-in-depth layer, not the control. Primary control is an ALLOWLIST: a new pure test file test/link-sites.test.js enumerates every .href= assignment in public/*.js (measured on master 7b1f036: 12 files, 9 assignments, 4 RHS shapes — dashHref(, tok.href, `?m=, serializeChatUrl( — 0 violations) and pins count 9 + RHS shape; plus a mechanism ban (setAttribute('href'), Object.assign( whole, ['href'], .href +=) and a .url/['url'] read ban across public/ (.url has zero consumers in public/ today). Spike (scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/AS-98/spike-guard.mjs) shows all 11 evasion spellings red — including two Ruben did not list (destructured url; host assembled from string fragments) that ONLY the allowlist catches — and the AS-115 span shape green. Threat model stated in §1: honest-mistake spellings, not adversarial evasion; §1.4 names what is out of scope and why. 11 ACs; 11 mutants (M1 = Ruben's M-M6 verbatim, predicted red {T7,T8,T10}; M6/M7/M9 allowlist-only reds {T8}; M11 is an expected-GREEN boundary demonstration with a revert re-red), each anchored to a named unique line per the 2026-09-10 sharpening. Baseline measured: host 542/541/0/1 skipped; compose -p asc-plan-as98 Built 542/535/0/7 skipped (torn down). Predicted branch tip: host 546/545/0/1, compose 546/539/0/7 (+4 tests). Seam with AS-115: its click-to-copy element is not an href site; M9 (cp.href='#' in bodyNode) is the spelling that turns it red; it may use setAttribute for role/tabindex but not Object.assign; merge order free. Seam with AS-88: no public/ overlap, both append to README in different sections, re-measure counts after whichever merges second. Slug feat/AS-98-href-allowlist-guard. Staffing: implementer developer-marcus; reviewer qa-priya (Ruben authored both the finding and the adopted tightenings — anchored twice; Priya gets plan+diff only, not review-AS-93.txt or my spike). No CLAUDE.md change, nothing for the board. 4 open questions time-boxed with defaults in §9.

Implementation done — HEAD 156faa5 on feat/AS-98-href-allowlist-guard (2 commits: f4ad8c2 tests, 156faa5 README). Ran on Opus (Fable fallback).

Built per plan §2: new apps/chat/test/link-sites.test.js — T8 enumerates every .href = assignment in public/*.js (12 files / 9 assignments), pins the count at 9, requires each RHS to begin with dashHref(, tok.href, `?m= or serializeChatUrl(; T9 mechanism ban (setAttribute('href', Object.assign(, ['href'], .href +=); T10 bans .url (except import.meta.url) and ['url'] reads; T11 drives the classifier with 9 rejected inputs, 4 allowed shapes (count 4, incl. the multi-line permalink head) and 1 comparison (count 0) — I read the plan's '5 accepted' as 4 allowed + the comparison. T7a whitespace-insensitive .url pattern; T7b literal list of six; comment updated to name link-sites.test.js as the primary control. README paragraph per §6 verbatim.

Counts (cardinality first): baseline was re-measured because AS-88 merged first (plan §5 warned): master post-AS-88 host 550/549/0/1 skipped. Branch host: 554 tests / 553 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped (+4 as predicted). Compose receipt, -p asc-impl-as98 --build, line quoted: 'Image asc-impl-as98-test Built' — 554 / 547 pass / 0 fail / 7 skipped (+4 over the 550/543/7 AS-88 review run). Project torn down (down -v --rmi local, network removed). Note: the compose file is apps/chat/compose.yaml, not docker-compose.yml.

Mutants (plan §3), HOST runs — 11 compose builds did not fit the 22-minute tick bound, so each mutant ran `node --test test/link-sites.test.js test/api.test.js` in the detached scratch worktree /tmp/AS-98-mutant (now removed); Priya's AC-10 runs are her own. Every mutant: marker 0->1, diff-stat one file (M11: two), anchor count 1->1 (M8: A-roster 1->0), restored with checkout, diff --exit-code clean. Anchors verified on the branch: A-panel app.js:718, A-roster :457, A-body 'function bodyNode(message) {' :254.
M1 {T7,T8,T10} as predicted. M2 {T9,T10} ✓ (T7/T8 green — the reason T9 exists). M3 {T9,T10} ✓. M4 {T7,T8} ✓. M5 {T7,T8} ✓. M6 {T8} only ✓. M7 {T8} only ✓. M8 {T7,T8,T10} ✓, T7 message names rosterRow. M9 {T8} only ✓. M10 {T9} only ✓. M11-revert (test restored, M6 kept) {T8} ✓. AC-5 extra ((?!=) removed from HREF_ASSIGN; comment occurrence left, regex occurrence gone) {T11} ✓.
FINDING — M11 wider than predicted: plan §3 predicts all GREEN by design; observed RED {T8, T11}. T8 because the M6 insertion is a tenth .href = assignment and the count pin (9) fires regardless of the loosened allowlist; T11 because the loosened /^url\b/ makes the rejected input 'shadow.href = url;' pass and the self-test counts it. I did not edit the prediction. Reading: the §1.4 boundary (destructured url read invisible to T10) is real, but the plan's claim that loosening the allowlist is the one silent edit is false in a good direction — the classifier self-test and the count pin both turn it red. Priya to confirm and decide whether the plan's M11 row should be corrected in a review-cycle note.
Driver + logs: scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/AS-98/{mutants.mjs,mutants.log,compose.log,progress.md}.

Left undone: nothing in scope. Worktree list = master + .worktrees/AS-98 (+ Lena's AS-115), AS-98 tree clean; no asc-as98-* images (host mutant runs built none). Merge seam per §7: AS-115 branch untouched by me.

REVIEW — AS-98 (qa-priya, tick watcher:86819 loop tick 13, on Opus per the Fable fallback). Branch feat/AS-98-href-allowlist-guard, head 156faa5 (f4ad8c2 tests, 156faa5 README). Diff read cold: 3 files, +161/-6 — link-sites.test.js (new, 145 lines), api.test.js T7a/T7b (13 lines), README (9 lines). Marcus's comment read AFTER my mutant runs, for his counts and the M11 deviation only.

VERDICT: PASS. 0 blocking findings. 4 findings outside the criteria list, all non-blocking (below). No inline fix committed — nothing in the diff is trivia-level wrong. Recommend done.

== FINDINGS FIRST (M5) ==

F1 (non-blocking, backlog) — a logical-assignment operator on a NEW anchor survives every guard. Probe P1: insert after A-panel `const p1 = el('a'); p1.href ||= task.taskId;` → 67/67 green, red set {}. HREF_ASSIGN matches only `=` and `+=` (`\+?=`), and the mechanism ban lists `.href +=` only, so `||=`, `??=`, `&&=` are invisible to T8/T9 and the count pin does not fire (the classifier never saw an assignment). Narrowed by P8: the same operator on an EXISTING site (`open.href ??= dashHref(...)` replacing A-panel) IS red {T7, T8} — the count drops 9→8 — so the survivor is only "added anchor + logical assignment". Classification: not an honest-mistake spelling for a fresh element (nobody writes `||=` on an element they just created), so it is a §1.4-class boundary, not a blocker. Cheapest close is one regex in MECHANISMS: `/\.href\s*(\|\||\?\?|&&)=/`. I am not making that inline — it changes what the guard catches, and the reviewer proving her own patch is the conflict this loop exists to prevent. Backlog task, or fold into the next touch of link-sites.test.js.

F2 (plan correction, non-blocking) — M11's §3 prediction ("all GREEN by design") is wrong; observed RED {T8, T11}, confirming Marcus. Two independent reasons, both in the guard's favour: (a) M6's insertion is a tenth `.href =`, and the count pin fires regardless of what ALLOWED_RHS says — so NO insertion mutant can ever demonstrate the boundary; (b) the loosened `/^url\b/` makes T11's rejected input `shadow.href = url;` pass, and the self-test counts it. So the "one silent edit" §1 describes is not silent: loosening the allowlist trips the classifier self-test, and the count pin has to be loosened in the same edit. The §1.4 boundary itself IS real — P7 (count-preserving: A-panel replaced by `const { url } = task; open.href = url;`) is red {T7, T8} only because T8's RHS check and T7's named-site assertion fire; T10 stays green on the destructured read, exactly as §1.4 says. To OBSERVE M11 as green you would need three edits (replace a site, loosen ALLOWED_RHS, and delete the T11 input), which is no longer a "casual" edit. Ruling: Marcus was right not to edit the prediction; the plan's §3 M11 row should get a correcting note from the orchestrator (as AS-93's §5 did), reading "observed {T8, T11}; the boundary is demonstrated by P7 not M11". Plan-level shape, but an error in a prediction table, not in the design — does not block.

F3 (housekeeping, fixed) — AC-11 says no `asc-as98-*` images remain; the implementer's comment says `asc-impl-as98` was torn down with `--rmi local`, but `asc-impl-as98-test:latest` (sha256:4959e282…) was still present when I checked. Attributable to Marcus's run by name, so I removed it (`docker rmi asc-impl-as98-test`, exit 0). No `/tmp/AS-98-*` left; `git worktree list` = master + AS-102 + AS-115 + AS-98 (the two siblings are other lanes, not mine).

F4 (boundary, recorded not blocking) — P2 `p2.href = dashHref(task.taskId) + '?x=' + task.url` on a new anchor is red {T7, T8, T10}, but T8 is red on the COUNT only: the RHS begins with `dashHref(` so the allowlist accepts a hand-appended tail. If the tail were a destructured `url` on a replaced site, only the named-site assertion in T7 would catch it, and only at one of the four named sites. Adversarial (§1.4), confirms the boundary; the allowlist is "begins with", and its English says so. No action.

Other probes, all red as the guard should: P3 RHS on the next line {T7, T8, T10}; P4 `/* comment */ task.url` {T8, T10} (T7a's pattern is broken by the comment — T8 is the control that survives it, which is the §1 argument holding); P5 `p5["href"] = …` double-quoted bracket {T9}; P6 `` `${location.origin}/x` `` — no literal, no .url — {T8}: the allowlist catches the hand-assembled origin that nothing else could.

== MUTANTS (M4 / AC-10) — my own runs, scratch worktree /tmp/AS-98-priya detached at 156faa5, host `node --test --test-reporter=tap test/link-sites.test.js test/api.test.js` (67 tests in the two guard files), NOT per-mutant compose builds (same choice Marcus made; the compose receipt below proves the image sees the same public/). Applied-assertion per run: marker 0→1, diff-stat names exactly the expected file(s), anchor count 1→1 (M8/P7/P8: anchor 1→0), `git checkout -- .` between runs, final scratch status empty. Runner and log: scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-98/mutants.mjs.

  M1  {T7, T8, T10}  as predicted (AC-1: Ruben's M-M6 verbatim, `shadow.href=task.url;`)
  M2  {T9, T10}      as predicted — T7 and T8 GREEN, quoted: the reason T9 exists
  M3  {T9, T10}      as predicted
  M4  {T7, T8}       as predicted (T10 green)
  M5  {T7, T8}       as predicted
  M6  {T8}           as predicted — every denylist green; the row that justifies §1
  M7  {T8}           as predicted
  M8  {T7, T8, T10}  as predicted; T7 message names rosterRow (AC-7)
  M9  {T8}           as predicted (the AS-115 seam spelling)
  M10 {T9}           as predicted
  M11 {T8, T11}      plan predicted GREEN — see F2; M11-revert (test restored, M6 kept) {T8} as predicted
  AC-5 extra ((?!=) removed from HREF_ASSIGN) {T11} as predicted
  11 plan runs + 1 revert + 1 AC-5 extra + 8 probes = 21 runs; 10 of 10 red-expected plan mutants red on EXACTLY the predicted set; 0 survivors among plan mutants; 1 survivor among my probes (F1).

== COUNTS, cardinality before quantification ==
Host, worktree apps/chat, `node --test`: 554 tests / 553 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped. Baseline master (previous tick) 550/549/1 → +4, as §5 predicts (four new tests, none removed, none retitled — verified in the diff).
Compose, `-p asc-review-as98 run --build --rm test`, receipt line quoted: `Image asc-review-as98-test Built` — 554 tests / 547 pass / 0 fail / 7 skipped (+4 over the 550/543/7 AS-88 review run). Torn down with `down --rmi local`; image removed; no asc-review-as98 image remains. T8 ran inside the image (the 12-file / 9-assignment classifier is wired to the served public/ the image copies — the vacuous-path check in §4).
Marcus's numbers (554/553/1 host; 554/547/7 compose) match mine.

== AS-115 SEAM (plan §7) — scratch check ==
In the scratch worktree: `git merge --no-commit --no-ff feat/AS-115-copy-refs` onto 156faa5 → clean, 0 conflicts (README and api.test.js auto-merged). Guard files on the merged tree: 67/67/0, red {}. Independent count of `.href =` assignments across the merged public/*.js: 9 — AS-115's copy chip adds no href site, as §7 requires. Merge aborted, scratch worktree removed. So AS-98 can merge first and AS-115's plan §7 expectation holds.

== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — floor check (11 of 11 pass; 4 findings OUTSIDE this list, above) ==
AC-1 PASS — M1 red {T7, T8, T10}, my run.
AC-2 PASS — T8 green on tip; M6/M7/M9 each red on exactly {T8}; P7 additionally proves the RHS check without the count pin.
AC-3 PASS — M2/M3 {T9, T10}, M10 {T9}.
AC-4 PASS — T10 in M1 and M8 red sets.
AC-5 PASS — T11 green on tip with 9 rejected / 4 allowed + 1 comparison (Marcus's reading of "5 accepted" is the sensible one; the message text says so); AC-5 extra red {T11}.
AC-6 PASS — T7 in M1 (spacing), M4/M5 (literals); literal list is the six named.
AC-7 PASS — M8 {T7, T8, T10}, T7 failure names rosterRow.
AC-8 PASS — counts above; §5's 546 was pre-AS-88 and the plan told the implementer to re-baseline; 550→554 is the +4.
AC-9 PASS — README paragraph present, verbatim §6, in the Links section after the `url`-field sentence.
AC-10 PASS — 21 runs recorded above with applied-assertions; M11 recorded as observed {T8, T11} (not expected-green — F2), revert re-red {T8}.
AC-11 PASS after F3 — no asc-*as98* images, no /tmp/AS-98-*, task worktree clean at 156faa5, the AS-10 server-side `url` assertions untouched (diff does not touch lattice.test.js; api.test.js edit is inside T7 only) and green in both runs.

§9 open questions: Q1 (destructured url in T10) — default "no" stands; P7 shows the href consequence is T8's, as argued. Q2 T7's .url pattern kept and widened — confirmed in the diff. Q3/Q4 nothing to add.

Process notes: I did not read scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus, scratchpad/agent-cto-owen or review-AS-93.txt; no Lattice auto-review artifact existed. My first mutant pass parsed the spec reporter and reported every red set as empty — a harness bug on my side, caught because M1 cannot be green; re-run with the TAP reporter. Recorded so nobody reads the first log (scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-98/) as a survivor sweep.

Not done / for the orchestrator: append the F2 correcting note to plan §3 M11; file F1 as a backlog task (one-regex widening of MECHANISMS to logical-assignment operators) or fold into the next link-sites edit. Status transition, merge, and board reply are Owen's.
